newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to raise forest products levy 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to raise forest products levy 10 pct.

text.p: Indonesia plans to raise by 10 percent the levy it imposes on forest products after increases in the price of plywood in the international market, the Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported on Saturday.
It quoted Forestry Minister Djamaludin Suryohadikusumo as saying the increase would be effective October 1.
"The ministerial decision will be issued possibly in the middle of September....because of the increase in the price of plywood," Djamaludin said.

The paper said the existing forest products levy (IHH) in Sumatra, Kalimantan, Sulawesi and Maluku was 23,500 rupiah ($10.03) per cubic metre for high-quality tree species used for sawn timber and 14,000 rupiah ($5.96) for jungle timber used for woodchips.
In Irian Jaya, Nusa Tenggara, Bali and East Timor the levy were 19,000 rupiah ($8.11) and 9,000 rupiah ($3.84), respectively.

Wood industry sources said this week that plywood prices in the key Japanese market had increased from $449.60 per cubic metre in April to $507.30 in June on the back of stronger demand for plywood in the Japanese construction sector.
